Set up, or check, the Python environment for the NumPyro / JAX engine

Source: R/python_env.R
setup_numpyro_env.Rd

Creates (or updates) a Python environment with jax and numpyro for jax_engine() and activates it for reticulate. With check_only = TRUE it only checks that the engine can run, and installs nothing.

Usage

setup_numpyro_env(
  envname = "r-numpyro-gpu",
  method = "auto",
  device = "auto",
  check_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

envname

Name of the conda or virtualenv environment. Default "r-numpyro-gpu".

method

"auto" (virtualenv), "virtualenv", or "conda".

device

"auto" (CUDA if nvidia-smi is found, otherwise CPU), "metal" (Apple Silicon), "cuda" (NVIDIA), or "cpu". Versions are pinned to tested combinations: jax==0.5.0 and numpyro==0.19.0 for CPU/CUDA; jax==0.4.34, jaxlib==0.4.34, jax-metal==0.1.1 for Metal. With check_only = TRUE, the device to check ("auto" uses the CPU on macOS).

check_only

Logical; only check whether the engine can run (see Details), without installing anything. Default FALSE.

Value

Invisible logical TRUE upon successful setup; with check_only = TRUE, a logical telling whether the engine is available.

Details

The check needs the package reticulate and a Python with the modules jax and numpyro. It uses the Python already initialised in the session, otherwise the one named by the environment variables RETICULATE_PYTHON or RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV, otherwise the r-numpyro-gpu environment created by this function (virtualenv, or conda when conda is on the PATH). When none of these exists it returns FALSE at once, without searching the system for other Python installations (which can take tens of seconds on some platforms). To use another Python, set RETICULATE_PYTHON, or select it with reticulate::use_python() and initialise it (e.g. reticulate::py_config()) before the check. The check never installs or downloads anything: the managed ('uv') Python of reticulate is not provisioned unless the RETICULATE_USE_MANAGED_VENV environment variable is set.

See also

jax_engine, hb_area

Examples

setup_numpyro_env(check_only = TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
setup_numpyro_env(device = "auto")
} # }
